tldr: This is not one event: three unrelated arXiv papers share the words "recurrent memory". It opened with the Dynamical Memory Transformer, which pairs attention with selective recurrent memories to keep per-token cost constant instead of growing with the KV cache.
whats_new: The latest paper (Nov 16) benchmarks memory capacity of variational quantum recurrent networks for time-series prediction, which is off the LLM-inference path entirely.
why_it_matters: Only the first two papers touch the long-context cost problem builders pay for: KV-cache growth versus fixed-size recurrent state in SSM-style models.

beats.headline: Dynamical Memory Transformer targets constant-cost attention
beats.summary: Hybrid design: keep attention's direct retrieval, but compress history into selective recurrent memories so per-token cost stops scaling with context length.

beats.headline: Representation theory questions diagonal SSM recurrences
beats.summary: Examines what linear recurrent memory can represent when implementations make the recurrence diagonal to keep the parallel scan cheap.

beats.headline: Quantum recurrent networks benchmarked on time-series memory
beats.summary: Shares the vocabulary, not the thread: a quantum ML benchmark with no bearing on LLM serving.

open_questions: Does the Dynamical Memory Transformer publish long-context retrieval results against a full-KV-cache baseline?
Does the diagonal-recurrence analysis lead to a concrete non-diagonal SSM variant with a parallel scan of comparable cost?
Does any inference engine ship support for a selective-recurrent-memory hybrid?
take_for_builders: No action: treat these as research to watch, and wait for released weights or a long-context eval before changing any KV-cache or model-choice plans.
